title: Take-over racing a wrong-person POST re-enters the correction loop — the wrong-person leg's first-failure UPDATE lacks the SQL taken_over_at guard the webhook leg has (r2-BLOCKER race residue)
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:1235 'case row.taken_over_at != "" {' ... 1250 'sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)' ; update_reference_call_status.sql:23-24 'WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status'
detail: taken_over_at is checked only on the request's read row; the UPDATE guards status alone, and take-over never changes status. A take-over landing between read and update leaves the row awaiting_correction + taken_over_at; correct then re-queues a row the sweep excludes forever (no un-take-over) — dead end, §8.6 impossible.
recommended_fix: Add AND taken_over_at IS NULL to the wrong-person leg's UPDATE (mirror mark_awaiting_correction.sql:17-18), or scope the call through a dedicated guarded query.

title: STILL PRESENT (r2): single-slot refcheck_edit — a second row's action choice or any action success still discards another row's in-progress typed trio
evidence: client.gleam:3397 'refcheck_edit: Some(prefill_refcheck_edit(' (RefcheckCorrect arm, unconditional overwrite) ; 3556 'refcheck_edit: None,' (success arm clears any open edit, no call_id match)
detail: UserChoseRefcheckAction Substitute/Correct overwrites any open edit from another row; any action success clears refcheck_edit unconditionally, dropping a different row's unsaved trio. Cancel now closes (half fixed); the discard halves remain.
recommended_fix: Guard the overwrite and the success-arm clear on edit.call_id == call_id (keep the open edit when it belongs to a different row), or key edits per call.
